claims.text: The initial material is an as-synthesized, chemically disordered, non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
Monte Carlo simulations can be integrated with first-principles magnetic exchange calculations to sample the magnetic free-energy landscape of non-equiatomic HEAs.
This computational scheme can manipulate the magnetic free-energy landscape.
First-principles calculations can describe finite-temperature magnetic behavior in a 3d-transition-metal HEA.
Local atomic configurations and chemical disorder modulate magnetic exchange interactions in the non-equiatomic HEA.
Free-energy sampling captures the interplay between random local chemical environments and magnetic interactions.
Accounting for finite-temperature magnetic fluctuations can materially affect calculated alloy energetics and phase stability.
The proposed sampling method can predict adjustments in magnetic transition temperatures.
The proposed sampling method can predict adjustments in magnetic entropy changes relevant to magnetocaloric behavior.
Using the computational method will enable controlled tuning of magnetic phase transitions in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Using the computational method will enable controlled tuning of the magnetocaloric response in non-equiatomic HEAs.
The proposed method will produce a measurable shift in magnetic transition temperature relative to conventional compositional tuning alone.
The proposed method will enhance the magnetocaloric effect by increasing magnetic entropy change relative to conventional compositional tuning alone.
The tuning effect requires retention of the chemically disordered state without significant phase separation.
Extreme magnetic fields or substantial deviations from the modeled local disorder may alter the predicted results.
